title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s White Day Part 5
text: Now that Filo and Keel’s performance had come to a close, I headed over to the Filolial Race venue. Over here, Midori from Motoyasu’s group is leading the effort to help out.

The main attraction is the King & Queen Cup, featuring a crossbreed between the Filolial variant I’m raising and the thoroughbred Motoyasu bred. There was some discussion about whether to enter Filo and the Tricolor Filolial in the exhibition race, but we’ve settled on deciding whether to do it based on how things go that day.

By the way, I’m just watching from the sidelines here, too. If I ride, the “Hero Bonus” kicks in, which counts as doping. If I were to ride Filo or any of the other Filolials, people would notice. Apparently, those in the know can spot it at a glance.

Also, apparently there are several types of Filolial races. One is a race where a jockey rides the Filolial, similar to horse racing in my world. This is the most common type, and it’s said that unless the Filolial and the jockey are in sync, they can’t achieve good results… or so I’ve heard.

Another type is a race without a jockey, where the Filolials run freely. In this case, they apparently compete using the “carrot-on-a-stick” method: a carriage is hitched to the back, and the winner is awarded a brand-new carriage. I’ve heard that Filolials are used in these races because they possess a certain level of intelligence.

There are also various other types of races, such as obstacle courses and battle races with intentional interference. In each of these, Filolials of various bloodlines are selected, and they compete against one another day in and day out—this is what the Filolial Races of Zeltoble are all about. Now, the newly established event is the King & Queen Cup, limited exclusively to Filolials raised by heroes. Since there’s almost no difference between male and female Filolials, it was decided to hold a combined race.

Even top-tier jockeys find them difficult to handle, and because they’re so unpredictable, the Filolials run on their own. At the starting gate, I can see the Filolials raised on my estate eagerly awaiting the starting signal. This race is a major highlight among Filolial races, and the spectators are passionately debating who will take first place. Since I’ve been watching the ones who practice every day lately, I can predict who’s likely to come out on top, but it seems hard for others to tell them apart. That said, the Filolial Race organizers are checking all the Filolials and seem to be putting together a betting sheet.

Ah, under our contract, a portion of the proceeds from these betting sheets goes into my pocket. According to the odds, the favorites seem to be the Filolials raised by Motoyasu. Apparently, their parents were famous Filolials.

It reminds me of that guy who came to the Filolial Ranch managed by Motoyasu. If I recall correctly… according to what Motoyasu’s three were translating, he came across as arrogant and unpleasant, didn’t he? Prioritizing speed, having a fiery temper, and being arrogant—how much is that, really?

Plus, he said something like he was so frustrated at losing to my Filolial that he wanted a rematch… I think it was after getting thoroughly beaten and feeling down that it was encouraged by its mate and managed to bounce back. That’s how Motoyasu’s Filolial was born. It takes after its parents—proud and hot-tempered.

Well, even so, it’s said to have a driven personality because it’s experienced losing to the villagers. A difficult personality, you might say? I heard in a report that while it’s capable of taking human form, it rarely does. It’s got pride, you see.
“Kue, kue-kue-kue.”
The rival to this guy is a variant of the Filolial I raised. This one… as I’ve mentioned before, is a glutton with no sense of tension. He’s a real mama’s boy.

But, you know… sometimes he acts even more eccentric than Filo. He’s dangerous in all sorts of ways. I’ve heard people say that being around him with Imiya gives them the chills, or that he’d lick them relentlessly. I wonder if it thinks I’m its prey? I thought that, but I didn’t say it.

By the way, this one can’t take human form, nor can it speak human language. It has various secrets, and I know a little about its origins. To be precise, it’s a monster that can’t really be called a Filolial… or something like that. I’ve made sure to properly inform the race organizers about that as well.

I was planning to gather the Raph-species that inhabit only my territory to hold a race… and apparently, this is one of those plans. Its popularity is average. Around here, the Filolials trained by Motoyasu are more famous, and Filo is rarely—or rather, never—entered into races. Chick is technically registered under my name, but since she has no interest in racing, she doesn’t compete either. Inevitably, rumors are circulating that the Filolials raised by the Spear Hero are more impressive than the Shield Hero who saved the world.
“I guess it’s about to start.”

I squint my eyes and look at the racetrack. This time, they’re using a fairly large racecourse. It’s a grass track, and I hear one lap is 2,800 meters. They say this race will cover a distance of 10 km—more than three laps around the track—which is a surprisingly long distance for horse racing.
Well, King & Queen are fast, after all. Maybe some people would understand if I compared it to F1. I don’t really get it myself, though.

If you apply F1 to the King & Queen Cup, the races just below that… are the ones where the original Filolials compete. At this distance, the race would be over in the blink of an eye. So, it seems they decided to extend the distance to test both speed and endurance. Since Motoyasu’s three Filolials are overseeing it, I’m sure it’ll be fine.
“Kue, Kue-Kue”

Huh? The thoroughbred Motoyasu raised is whispering something to the mutant I raised. The other Filolials around us are furrowing their brows as they watch the exchange. The mutant blinks slightly, tilts its head, and chirps something like “Kue?” What on earth are they talking about?

Well… looks like it’s about to start. The referee is holding the flag high, its end in hand. Both the Filolials and the spectators are holding their breath, eagerly awaiting the start. With a sharp wave of the flag, the gate opens, and the Filolials burst out at the same time.
Oh? The Filolial Motoyasu raised has pulled off a great start and shot to the front. On the other hand, the one I raised is in last place. It’s running at its own pace.

As the Filolials ran, the grass beneath their feet was being torn up, leaving bald patches in their wake. Just how much power are they putting into their legs? Or rather… the spectators aren’t cheering—they’re speechless.
“T-they’re fast!”
“I never imagined there’d be such a difference in speed!”
“This is… the dawn of a new era in Filolial racing!”

Voices like these could be heard from all around. Apparently, they’ve never had just the King and Queen race before. That’s why the Filolials from Motoyasu’s group never used to run at full speed against opponents who weren’t the King or Queen; they’d just maintain a certain distance in the lead. To put it bluntly, they were holding back.
But this time is different. Their opponents are fast too, and if they hold back, they’ll get left behind. That’s why everyone’s running at full speed… or so it seems.

They’re definitely fast. Everyone is accelerating using “Petit Quick” and “High Quick,” moves that Filo uses often. You can tell just by watching from a distance. But… I’m riding on Filo’s back, and he’s running even faster than that… Isn’t he faster than a car?

As for the race itself, it seems the Thoroughbreds are running while conserving their stamina so they don’t use it all up, even in short races. Since their base speed is so high, even when they’re holding back, the other Filolials are barely keeping up. I guess this is the moment when a child fulfills the unfulfilled dream of their parent? Though I’ve heard that even that parent, after receiving a monster crest under Motoyasu’s guidance, was able to transform and overtake them to some extent. Come to think of it… since “Queenification” is an acquired ability, wouldn’t someone with innate excellence surpass them if they transformed?

But… there’s also the case of Filo, so maybe you can’t generalize. A Filolial with a base value equivalent to 100 silver coins is the fastest. You never know what’ll happen with King and Queen transformations. If that’s the kind of creature’s offspring, the mystery only deepens… I suppose.

According to Rat, based on the results of my—somewhat deranged—research, if a Hero raises a Filolial, the Filolial’s genes activate aspects that were previously unknown. In short, simply being raised by a Hero transforms them into exceptional individuals, and their potential can no longer be determined by bloodline alone.

Oh, the race has reached the midway point. Around this time, some Filolials start dropping out because they can’t keep up with the pace. If they fall a lap behind, they’re disqualified. But—perhaps because I’d ordered them not to push themselves too hard—those who felt their stamina reaching its limit quickly moved to the edge of the track and collapsed. It’s a brutal battle… It looks like some have even lost consciousness.

I see someone watching this, throwing their ticket into the air and yelling, “Don’t give up!” I guess you’d want to say that… but I want you to acknowledge that the Filolial you believed in gave it its absolute all. It’s on a whole different level.

Even if you’re naturally fast, there’s always someone faster. They’re pushing themselves to the point of coughing up blood, trying to determine who’s the fastest at Motoyasu’s Filolial Ranch. Being fast isn’t the only measure of worth. Among them are those skilled in combat and those who excel at pulling carriages. There’s even one who learned how to make chocolate and joined the cooking group. I plan to give rewards to those who gave it their all later on.

Wait… why am I getting so emotionally invested? That said, it’s a bit of a mixed feeling to have my Filolials complain to me. They’re the kind who put on a show and only meow “Quest” in front of me… but I’ll give them credit for their effort.

And then… as the race neared its final stretch. The mutant I’d raised—who’d been plodding along slowly until then, currently in last place yet, strangely enough, running at a steady pace without falling a lap behind—suddenly opened its eyes wide and leaned forward.
“Kueeeeeeeeeee!”

It spread its brown tail feathers—with a black tip—and lay them flat… puffing out its feathers as it was engaged in the process of Gathering Magical Power into its body. The remnants of that power began to glow, sending beams of light shooting backward.
